bounded_entry_proposal.collision: tag mismatch replaces direct-indexed record with count1 for current tile
bounded_entry_proposal.trigger: same tag+tile and old_count<9 and new_count==9; fresh record starts1; hold count9 thereafter

distance.fidelity: 64-bit payload cannot contain tag plus full tile32+count32. Proposed tag28/tile32/count4 packing preserves threshold9 decisions for resident records but collisions lose history, unlike simulator unordered_map. It is an explicit bounded hardware design, not a claim of full simulator equivalence; hardware.json geometry and simulator remain unchanged.
distance.implementation: metadata RMW sequencer,adder32/64,register/FSM,tag/tile/count compare,mux; forward-neighbour address helper; SRAM remains separately priced
distance.ports: L1 demand touch(line64,tile32),metadata64 read/write,index13; trigger/retrigger; layer stride/radix; candidate64,valid
transitions: every demand L1 probe, including L1 hit/reprobe, is a touch
lazy reset on changed tile; increment count; touch trigger iff post-increment==9
on_demand without retrigger requires count>=9; retrigger bypasses this filter
emit one forward COUT neighbour iff target block within extent
production touch mode disables L2 miss/retrigger firing; miss mode is separately supported

neighbour.boundary: khkw_split indexing is a separate shared address helper; characterize it separately from one adder if including decode, rather than claim the existing adder-only row prices it.
neighbour.contract: stride=ceil(CIN/16)*min(8,KH*KW); radix=ceil(COUT/4); block=(line/stride)%radix; valid=(block+1<radix),target=line+stride. Config B neighbour up-only d1 uses same arithmetic at both levels.
neighbour.implementation: adder64,compare,mux; decode via finite restoring divide/remainder built from adder/compare/register or specialize layer constants; no divider library primitive needed

next_access.bounds: 32-bit nonnegative tile/burst ids; finite descriptor port is supplied by schedule/trace address generator, not predicted from current address. Current burst/end counters are explicit controller glue; no per-entry burst-tag array if one burst drains at a time. No4x64B data buffer.
next_access.implementation: adder32/64,register32,common fifo64x4,equality/max/boundary mux,FSM/status; persistent three state words are input/output ports of logic top and priced separately
next_access.persistent_state: per core pf_cursor32=0,last_tile32=-1,last_burst32=-1; existing next_access_state row owns these words
next_access.ports: demand_valid,tile32,k32,n_bursts32; indexed future-burst descriptor/expanded-line stream(line64,last_line); candidate64; resident,inflight,budget_ok; whole_burst_handled,abort
next_access.separation: cache-tag/MSHR probes, credits and ports are engine inputs, already separately accounted. FIFO streaming preserves order but circuit cycle equivalence is not claimed.
next_access.state_encoding: store complemented last_tile/last_burst so existing zero-reset register decodes logical-1; pf_cursor is plain zero-reset; no extra persistent valid bit
transitions: tile-start resets all three state words
suppress repeated(tile,k), then remember current pair
cursor=max(cursor,k+1); visit cursor..min(k+4,n_bursts-1)
stream mapper-expanded distinct increasing lines one burst at a time through4x64 address queue
resident/MSHR redundancy drops count as handled; budget refusal aborts remaining batch
advance cursor only on fully handled burst; partial burst keeps cursor until next demand pull-forward
